idiom_name: kotlinx.serialization sealed hierarchy with a class discriminator
implementation_notes: kotlinx.serialization is the default JSON story on Kotlin: mark the base sealed class or interface @Serializable, give each subtype a @SerialName (the tag value) and let Json emit the class discriminator - "type" by default, configurable globally with Json { classDiscriminator = "..." } or per hierarchy with @JsonClassDiscriminator. Sealed hierarchies are closed, so the generated serializer's subtype list is the allow-list; for open hierarchies register each implementation explicitly with polymorphic { subclass(...) } in a SerializersModule (subclassesOfSealed() registers a sealed hierarchy in bulk). The handwritten factory is unnecessary while the hierarchy is sealed; it returns when the tag must differ from @SerialName or the mapping must be data-driven.
pitfalls: The discriminator is written only when the declared type is the base type and ClassDiscriminatorMode.POLYMORPHIC is active: serializing a concrete-typed property omits the tag, so a later read through the base type fails.
An unknown discriminator makes decodeFromString throw SerializationException with no unknown-type bucket of its own, so catch it at the boundary and quarantine the payload.
@JsonClassDiscriminator is marked @ExperimentalSerializationApi and @SerialName values are the wire contract: pin the library version and treat renames as format changes.
